question: Which of these is a core duty for a nurse managing a high-risk labour?

options.C: It eliminates the need for any documentation to travel with the patient

explanation: Calling ahead gives the team time to prep the operating room and blood bank so treatment starts the second the ambulance arrives. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h7)

question: What is the main goal of the Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) model in public hospitals?

options.A: To replace state government health budgets entirely
options.B: To fund free housing for incoming medical staff
options.C: To ensure a steady supply of essential medicines
options.D: To generate heavy profit for hospital management

explanation: You've got this! The DRF uses money from drug sales strictly to restock those same drugs, keeping our pharmacy shelves stocked so we never run out unexpectedly. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h1)

question: Which of these is one of the classic stages of grief identified by Elisabeth Kübler-Ross?

options.A: Detachment
options.B: Bargaining
options.C: Resolution
options.D: Isolation

explanation: Spot on! Bargaining is a well-known stage where a person tries to negotiate a way out of the painful reality, like saying 'God, if you heal them, I will change my ways.' [learn more](GNS321_U4_T9#GNS321_U4_T9_h3)

question: What term describes the overlap between personal and organisational objectives?

options.A: Institutional friction
options.B: Operational burnout
options.C: Goal congruence
options.D: Budget deficit

explanation: 'Goal congruence' just means working in harmony—it's when your personal goals match up nicely with the hospital's goals. [learn more](GST321_U2_T2#GST321_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why is it important to write down any learning barriers (like poor eyesight or hearing) in the nursing notes?

options.A: It replaces the need for verbal handovers between shifts
options.B: It allows the hospital to charge extra fees for communication
options.C: It guides incoming nurses on how to adapt future teaching sessions
options.D: It proves the patient was difficult and uncooperative

explanation: Documenting barriers helps the whole nursing team communicate effectively without making the patient repeat themselves. Excellent teamwork! [learn more](GNS215_U4_T7#GNS215_U4_T7_h8)

question: How does a non-judgmental attitude from a nurse directly improve reproductive healthcare outcomes?

options.A: It allows the clinic to reduce its security staff budget
options.B: It guarantees that the client will never experience medical complications
options.C: It speeds up the discharge process for postpartum mothers
options.D: It encourages clients to share accurate history and seek help early

explanation: When clients feel accepted rather than judged, they are more honest about their symptoms and seek care before problems escalate. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T1#GNS312_U5_T1_h5)

question: You are assessing a patient with a newly created AV fistula in their arm. What finding tells you it is open and working well?

options.A: A palpable thrill and audible bruit over the fistula site
options.B: Absence of any sound or vibration when listening with a stethoscope
options.C: A cool hand with weak pulses past the surgical site
options.D: A strong pulse with severe pain and redness in the fingers

explanation: You'll love listening for this in the ward! When arterial and venous blood rush together, it creates a gentle vibration (thrill) and a swishing sound (bruit) that confirms good blood flow. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h7)

question: Which of the following is an example of health advocacy by a nurse?

options.A: Refusing to care for patients from different tribes
options.B: Prescribing antibiotics independently without a doctor
options.C: Keeping all hospital supply records a strict secret
options.D: Speaking up about dangerous staff shortages on the ward

explanation: Advocacy involves defending patient safety and speaking out against systemic issues that compromise care quality. [learn more](GST321_U6_T3#GST321_U6_T3_h7)

question: Which of these medications is classified as a long-acting corticosteroid?

options.A: Prednisolone
options.B: Dexamethasone
options.C: Hydrocortisone
options.D: Methylprednisolone

explanation: Correct! Dexamethasone is a long-acting steroid that stays active in the body for 36 to 72 hours. Keep up the great revision! [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h2)

question: What main activity happens inside the body during the incubation period?

options.A: Rapid multiplication of the germs inside the body
options.B: Rapid production of red blood cells
options.C: Complete destruction of germs by normal skin oils
options.D: Immediate slowing down of the nervous system

explanation: Think of it like seeds growing quietly before sprouting. Pathogens multiply and grow in number until there are enough to make the person feel sick! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T84#GNS214_U1_T84_h2)

question: What exactly is water pollution?

options.A: The natural filtration of rainwater through soil layers
options.B: The contamination of water sources by harmful substances
options.C: The evaporation of clean water from surface reservoirs
options.D: The normal movement of minerals from rocks into rivers

explanation: Spot on! Water pollution happens when harmful agents find their way into natural water bodies, making them unsafe for use. [learn more](GST114_U6_T6#GST114_U6_T6_h1)
